subject: Recap: Redwood vs Hyperscaler benchmarks & test plan
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@globex.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@globex.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 28 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Recap: Redwood vs Hyperscaler benchmarks & next steps

Thanks for the time today — great conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned: 

Summary of what we heard from Globex
- Primary goal: improve inference latency for real-time features (customer chat & summarization).
- Target SLOs you called out: p95 ~300ms and p99 ~600ms (we’ll confirm exactly in your reply).
- Throughput target: sustained ~800 tokens/sec for the core chat workload (peak bursts higher).

What Redwood proposes for the evaluation
- A/B benchmark comparing Redwood Dedicated (pinned capacity) vs your current hyperscaler-managed endpoint.
- Test matrix: model variants (FP16 vs 4-bit quantized), batching profiles, and warm/cold cache runs.
- Metrics we’ll collect: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec (steady-state), error rate, and cost-per-1M tokens.

Attachments & links
- I’m attaching a short test plan and the baseline latency CSV we collected last week. Full test plan is also on Drive: https://drive.google.com/redwood/globex/testplan-20260301

Proposed next steps
1) Confirm targets (p95/p99 and throughput) and any guardrails for error rates or timeouts.
2) Approve test window (we propose Mar 4–5 for the A/B runs).
3) Share any internal test accounts / IP allowlist for Redwood to hit (or tell us if you prefer we run from our end against your endpoint).

If that all sounds right I’ll schedule the runs and loop in Marcus to own the execution and data capture.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | (415) 555-0142

--

Attachment: redwood-globex-benchmarks-202602.csv (csv)

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@globex.com>

Date: Sat, 28 Feb 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Recap: Redwood vs Hyperscaler benchmarks & next steps

Thanks Marissa — helpful recap. A few clarifications from our side:
- Confirmed targets: p95 < 300ms, p99 < 600ms for the chat path. If Redwood can meet that consistently we’ll have a strong case.
- Throughput: 800 tokens/sec steady-state per core flow is our current target; peak bursts of ~1.5k tokens/sec are expected (short spikes).
- Data residency: Globex requires EU residency for certain PII flows; for the initial bench you can run from your hosted region but for production we’ll need a private deployment or dedicated EU pool.

Also: can you confirm whether your dedicated offering will run the same model family we currently use (latest open checkpoint) and whether 4-bit quantization will be evaluated side-by-side?

Priya — looping you in to confirm test contacts & any IP allowlist.

— Alex
Alex Johnson
Sr. Platform Eng, Globex
alex.johnson@globex.com | (617) 555-0101

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 1 Mar 2026 08:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Recap: Redwood vs Hyperscaler benchmarks & next steps

Hi Alex — thanks, all noted. Short answers then proposed test matrix below.

Model parity and quantization
- We’ll run the same open checkpoint family you’re using (we’ll confirm exact commit/hash once you share it).
- Test runs will include FP16 and 4-bit quantized variants (end-to-end) so you can compare latency/quality tradeoffs.

Residency
- For the benchmark you mentioned it’s fine to run from our hosted region; we’ll also provide a plan for an EU-dedicated pool for later stages.

Proposed test matrix (attached spreadsheet)
- A/B split: 50/50 traffic allocation (controlled load generator)
- Variants: Hyperscaler endpoint (baseline), Redwood Dedicated FP16, Redwood Dedicated 4-bit
- Warmup: 30 minutes sustained load to prime KV cache, then 2 hours steady-state capture
- Metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec (steady-state), percent timeouts, cost estimate per 1M tokens

We’ll run the baseline at the times you approved (Mar 4–5). Marcus will lead execution and share raw CSVs and a summary deck after the runs.

Link to test plan & proposal: https://drive.google.com/redwood/globex/testplan-20260301

Thanks — attaching the test plan & baseline CSV again.

Marissa

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>

Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Mar 2026 10:20:00 -0800
Subject: Benchmark run details and warmup plan

Alex / team — quick technical notes from the execution side so there are no surprises during the window: 

Execution plan
- We’ll provision a dedicated pool equivalent to the committed shape for the test (pins model + instance type).
- Warmup script: 30-minute ramp with representative prompt mix (seed set in the attached params file). Warmup ensures KV cache is populated and batching stabilizes.
- Two runs per variant: cold-start (no cache) and warm (post-warmup). We’ll report both.

Metrics collection and confidence intervals
- We’ll capture request-level logs and compute p50/p95/p99 latencies along with tokens/sec. We’ll also compute 95% bootstrap CI on p95/p99 to show run variability.

Quantization notes
- 4-bit quantization typically reduces p50/p95 by ~15-35% depending on kernel selection and sequence lengths; we’ll report quality delta on a small eval set you provide.

Attachments: benchmark-run-params.txt (contains seed prompts, batch sizes, concurrency targets).

If you want us to run the tests from within your VPC instead (to remove network variance) we can coordinate on IP allowlist + short-lived creds. Otherwise we’ll run from Redwood Dedicated in us-west and note network hops in the analysis.

— Marcus
